The must-sees

  • Büyük Han

    Shopping · 1572

    Lala Mustafa Pasha, the first Ottoman governor of Cyprus, had it built in 1572. It served travellers and merchants, and today its rooms hold craft shops and cafés.

    Look for: The little courtyard mosque stands raised on pillars over a fountain, so travellers could wash before prayer.

  • Cyprus Museum

    Museum

    It was founded in 1882 under British rule. Its galleries run from prehistoric figurines to a crowd of terracotta votive figures from the sanctuary at Agia Irini.

    Look for: Find the marble Aphrodite of Soli, the goddess found at the ancient city of Soli on the island’s northwest coast.

  • Green Line

    Landmark

    The line was first drawn at the end of 1963 during intercommunal violence, and became a UN-patrolled buffer zone after 1974. The south is run by the Republic of Cyprus, the north by a Turkish Cypriot administration only Turkey recognises.

    Look for: Through gaps in the barriers, see abandoned shopfronts, faded signs and weeds growing where streets once ran busy.

  • Ledra Street

    Shopping

    In the 1950s, during the fight against British rule, it was called the Murder Mile. It was barricaded during the violence of 1963–64, and a crossing for pedestrians opened at its northern end in 2008.

    Look for: Look up at the Shacolas Tower, the tallest block on the street, whose upper floor has long served as a lookout over both halves of the city.

  • Selimiye Mosque

    Building

    Built as the Cathedral of St Sophia, it was consecrated in 1326, and the Lusignan kings of Cyprus were crowned here. After the Ottoman conquest of 1570 it became a mosque, and it is still in use.

    Look for: Inside, the Gothic nave is whitewashed and the carpets run at an angle across it, turned toward Mecca rather than the old altar.

  • Venetian Walls

    Fortress

    The Venetians built them from 1567, with eleven bastions, to defend against the Ottomans. The walls were not enough: the city fell in 1570 after a siege of about seven weeks.

    Look for: Walk through the Famagusta Gate, the old eastern entrance, a long vaulted passage cut through the rampart.

How it works

  1. Open Wizzy in Nicosia and tap Start walk, or pick a ready-made walk.
  2. Put your phone in your pocket. Wizzy runs in the background, even with the screen locked.
  3. When you pass a place, you get a ping. Open it for the story, or keep walking.

Every place you see gets stamped in your Nicosia passport. Your location stays on your phone. No ads, no tracking.
